channel_up.description: Next channel in the current channel list.

close_app.description: Close a running app by id.

insert_text.description: Type text into the focused field, replacing the selection.

launch_app.description: Launch an installed app by id. Optional payload keys params (object) and contentId (string) deep-link into the app.

mute_on.description: Mute. setMute takes an explicit bool, so on and off are separate commands; a toggle reads ssap://audio/getStatus first.

open_channel.description: Tune a channel by id. Ids come from ssap://tv/getChannelList; the current channel from ssap://tv/getCurrentChannel.

channel_id.description: channelId from the channel list — opaque, not the channel number.

power_off.description: Standby. The socket dies with the TV; don't wait for the reply.

press_info.description: Info — details for the focused item/channel.

press_ok.description: OK — activate the focused item. The wire name is ENTER; there is no separate OK.

screen_off.description: Blank the panel but keep the TV running (audio keeps playing). webOS 4+; older sets used the removed com.webos.service.tv.power/turnOffScreen.

volume.description: Percent of the TV's volume scale.

show_toast.description: Pop a short text message on screen. Optional payload keys iconData/iconExtension attach a base64 icon, which newer firmware silently ignores.

device.name: LG webOS TV Second Screen Protocol
device.notes: Control is a WebSocket to port 3000 (ws) with a required fallback to 3001 (wss, self-signed certificate) — late firmware refuses the plain socket entirely. On the socket the client sends a hello frame, then a register frame carrying a pairing manifest; on first contact the TV shows an accept prompt and answers with a client-key, which authenticates every later connection. Commands are JSON request frames naming SSAP URIs (ssap://system/turnOff, ssap://audio/volumeUp, ssap://tv/channelDown, ssap://system.launcher/launch, ssap://com.webos.applicationManager/listApps); remote-button presses go over a SECOND WebSocket, the pointer input socket, as plain-text frames (type:button\nname:HOME). Discovery is SSDP only: ST urn:lge-com:service:webos-second-screen:1 gives a LOCATION whose XML carries UDN, serialNumber, friendlyName and modelName. There is no power-on command — ssap://system/turnOn was removed from firmware — so wake is Wake-on-LAN, gated by an on-TV setting whose name varies by model year (Mobile TV On / Turn On Via WiFi / IP control Wake on LAN). The TV must have "LG Connect Apps" enabled (Network settings; "Mobile App" on older firmware) or pairing never prompts.

openness.notes: LG publishes SDKs (Connect SDK; webOSTV.js for on-TV apps) but no protocol document for the second-screen socket, so the status stays undocumented even though LG's own open-source client is among the sources. The parts reconstructed rather than read from anything LG published: the ports and the ws→wss fallback, the hello frame newer firmware expects, the pointer-socket text-frame format, and the per-firmware gaps (pointer socket inert on webOS 1.x, plain ws refused late) — all from community client source.

upstream_docs.covers: LG's own reference implementation of the protocol — discovery, the pairing manifest, and the SSAP calls. LG never published a wire-format document; this source is the closest thing to one.

issued_to_client: client-key — 32-hex pairing token returned in the registered message
credentials.notes: The WiFi passphrase is typed on the TV itself, so no protocol here carries it. The secret that matters is the client-key: anything holding it has full control until it is revoked on the TV. First pairing cannot happen silently — the PROMPT pairing type requires a human at the screen — but an accepted client-key is bearer credentials from then on.

factory_reset.effect: Clears network credentials, the LG account link, installed apps, the paired-device list (every issued client-key) and all settings; the TV returns to the first-run wizard.

steps.action: Settings > All Settings > General > System > Reset to Initial Settings (menu path varies slightly by webOS version).
steps.notes: There is no recessed reset button on the TV; the menu path is the only documented procedure. To revoke one paired client without resetting, remove it from the TV's paired-device list under the LG Connect Apps / device-connection settings.

methods.description: First-run wizard on the TV (language, network, passphrase on the on-screen keyboard, optional LG account), then an on-TV toggle that permits second-screen pairing at all.

steps.action: Power on the TV and complete the first-run wizard with the remote: language, then WiFi network and passphrase.
steps.expect: TV reports a successful network connection.

steps.action: Enable second-screen control: Settings > Network > LG Connect Apps = On (older firmware: Settings > General > Mobile App; the name varies by webOS version).

Discover the TV by SSDP and open the control socket (ws://<ip>:3000, falling back to wss://<ip>:3001), then send the hello frame, a ssap://system/getSystemInfo request, and the register frame with pairingType PROMPT and no client-key (wire format per webos_common.handshake).
steps.expect: The TV shows an accept/decline prompt for the new device.

steps.action: Accept the pairing prompt on the TV screen.
steps.expect: The socket delivers a second message of type registered whose payload carries the client-key.

steps.action: Store the client-key and include it in the register payload on every later connection.
steps.expect: register answers immediately with no prompt.

setup.notes: Onboarding happens on the TV's own screen; no credential crosses any protocol this file documents. What a client must survive is PAIRING, which is part of the control protocol itself: first register gets an on-screen prompt, acceptance returns a client-key, and the TV remembers it until the paired-device list is cleared or the TV is reset. Confidence is medium: the flow below is what aiowebostv, bscpylgtv and openHAB all implement against production TVs, but this project has not replayed it.

rejoin.notes: Settings > Network re-runs only the network step; pairing and client-keys survive a router change. A factory reset is never needed just to move networks.

entities.name: Power Off
entities.notes: Power-on is Wake-on-LAN, not a button this file can offer.

entities.name: OK
entities.notes: Pointer-socket button; the wire name is ENTER.

entities.name: Volume
entities.notes: Internal speakers only; with external audio, use the step buttons.

entities.name: Input
entities.notes: Options come from ssap://tv/getExternalInputList (field "devices", appId per input); the current input is the foreground app (getForegroundAppInfo) when it is a com.webos.app.* input app. Both reads are SSAP queries, so this picker awaits the WebSocket transport like everything else here.

entities.name: App
entities.notes: Options come from ssap://com.webos.applicationManager/listLaunchPoints (field "launchPoints", id/title per app; listApps adds hidden apps), current selection from getForegroundAppInfo.appId. Selecting an option IS launching it.

entities.name: Foreground App
entities.notes: appId of the foreground app; also the Live TV tell (com.webos.app.livetv).

entities.name: Current Channel
entities.notes: Meaningful only while Live TV is foreground.

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder for the SSAP service on ports 3000 (ws) and 3001 (wss). A plain GET here is only the WebSocket upgrade; every real exchange is JSON frames per webos_common. Recorded so the access surface names the port, not because any REST endpoint exists.
http_endpoints.name: webOS Second Screen WebSocket

connection.description: One TCP port, two spellings: ws://<ip>:3000 is the original listener and what older firmware expects; wss://<ip>:3001 is the TLS listener late firmware demands. aiowebostv's rule — try plain ws on 3000, and on connection refusal or a rejected upgrade fall back to wss on 3001 — is the one to copy. The 3001 certificate is self-signed; clients disable verification (aiowebostv passes ssl=False), so TLS here buys obfuscation, not authentication — authentication is the client-key. WebSocket-level ping/pong heartbeat (~5s) keeps the session up.

handshake.description: The first frames on a fresh socket, in aiowebostv's order. (1) hello: {"id":"hello","type":"hello","payload":{}} — the TV answers type "hello" with protocol metadata (and a deviceUUID). (2) A pre- registration ssap://system/getSystemInfo request, which newer webOS versions require before registration and older ones simply tolerate. (3) register: {"id":"register_0","type":"register","payload":{...}} — the payload below, plus "client-key": <stored key> once paired (null or absent before). With pairingType PROMPT and no valid key the TV shows an on-screen accept prompt; the register first answers type "response" echoing the pairingType, then — only if the user accepts — a second message of type "registered" whose payload carries the client-key. A declined or timed-out prompt answers type "error".

register_payload.description: The exact registration payload every open client sends (aiowebostv handshake.py, identical in ancestry to Connect SDK's). The `signed` block is boilerplate — the same static appId and RSA signature in every client since Connect SDK; the TV does not validate it against any store. The permissions list is what the TV enforces later: an SSAP call outside it answers "401 insufficient permissions".
register_payload.example:
{
  "forcePairing": false,
  "pairingType": "PROMPT",
  "manifest": {
    "manifestVersion": 1,
    "appVersion": "1.1",
    "permissions": [
      "LAUNCH", "LAUNCH_WEBAPP", "APP_TO_APP", "CLOSE",
      "TEST_OPEN", "TEST_PROTECTED", "CONTROL_AUDIO",
      "CONTROL_DISPLAY", "CONTROL_INPUT_JOYSTICK",
      "CONTROL_INPUT_MEDIA_RECORDING", "CONTROL_INPUT_MEDIA_PLAYBACK",
      "CONTROL_INPUT_TV", "CONTROL_POWER", "CONTROL_TV_SCREEN",
      "READ_APP_STATUS", "READ_CURRENT_CHANNEL",
      "READ_INPUT_DEVICE_LIST", "READ_NETWORK_STATE",
      "READ_RUNNING_APPS", "READ_TV_CHANNEL_LIST",
      "WRITE_NOTIFICATION_TOAST", "READ_POWER_STATE",
      "READ_COUNTRY_INFO", "CONTROL_INPUT_TEXT",
      "CONTROL_MOUSE_AND_KEYBOARD", "READ_INSTALLED_APPS",
      "READ_SETTINGS"
    ],
    "signed": {
      "appId": "com.lge.test",
      "created": "20140509",
      "vendorId": "com.lge",
      "localizedAppNames": {"": "LG Remote App"},
      "localizedVendorNames": {"": "LG Electronics"},
      "permissions": ["TEST_SECURE", "CONTROL_INPUT_TEXT", "..."],
      "serial": "2f930e2d2cfe083771f68e4fe7bb07"
    },
    "signatures": [{"signatureVersion": 1, "signature": "<static Connect SDK signature; copy from aiowebostv handshake.py>"}]
  }
}

input_channel.description:
Remote-button presses do NOT go over SSAP. Request ssap://com.webos.service.networkinput/getPointerInputSocket on the main socket; the response payload's socketPath is a second WebSocket URL on the same ports. Open it and send plain-text frames (not JSON), key:value lines terminated by a blank line: 'type:button
name:HOME

' for a button, 'type:move
dx:5
dy:0
down:0

' for pointer motion, 'type:click

' and 'type:scroll
dx:0
dy:-120

' for the Magic Remote's pointer. Known button names (openHAB's list, compiled by trial across models): LEFT RIGHT UP DOWN ENTER (the OK button) BACK EXIT HOME INFO, the digits 0-9 spelled as themselves, RED GREEN YELLOW BLUE, PLAY PAUSE STOP. The socket is accepted but inert on the earliest webOS 1.x sets (2014-2015, UF series and earlier) — a firmware limitation, not a client bug; on those models only the SSAP commands work.

power.False: ssap://system/turnOff — a normal request frame; the TV drops the socket as it shuts down, so do not wait for the response.
power.True: There is no network power-on: ssap://system/turnOn is listed by bscpylgtv among the URIs firmware removed. Wake is Wake-on-LAN — a magic packet to the subnet broadcast — and it is gated on the TV: Settings > General > Mobile TV On > Turn On Via WiFi on 2017+ models, Settings > Support > IP control settings > Wake on LAN on 2025+ models; it works most reliably over Ethernet. Capture the MAC from the SSDP description or the TV's network info while it is on.

request_format.description: After registration, every command is one JSON text frame: {"id": <int>, "type": "request", "uri": "ssap://<service>/<method>", "payload": {...}}. id is a client-chosen integer that matches request to response; payload is {} when the URI takes no arguments. type is "subscribe" instead of "request" for live state — the TV then keeps pushing type "response" frames on the same id until "unsubscribe". In `commands` below, `action` is the uri (minus the ssap:// prefix's scheme — it is spelled in full anyway) and `arguments` is the payload.

response_format.description: Success: {"id": <same>, "type": "response", "payload": {"returnValue": true, ...}} with the result fields beside returnValue (volumeUp has none; listLaunchPoints adds "launchPoints": [{"id": "netflix", "title": "Netflix", ...}]). Failure: type "error" with an error string — "404 no such service or method" (URI absent on this firmware), "401 insufficient permissions" (outside the manifest), "500 Application error". Treat a missing URI as capability absent, not as connection failure.
